requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: An RSA 4096-bit self-signed X.509 certificate was generated on node1 with Subject=Issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison, and Basic Constraints CA:TRUE, confirming a valid self-signed root CA was created.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: The CA cert was copied into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and update-ca-trust extract was run; trust list subsequently shows the 'OS Comparison Root CA' label as a trusted certificate, and openssl verify against the system CA bundle returns OK, directly confirming system-wide trust.

requirements.requirement: Trust store actually honors the new CA (functional validation, not just presence)
requirements.summary: A leaf certificate signed by the new CA was verified against the system CA bundle and returned OK, demonstrating the trust chain is functionally honored, not merely configured.

requirements.requirement: CA trust configuration survives a node restart (provider-wide restart-evidence protocol, not part of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (2fc81aed...) and healthy CA trust state were captured, a shutdown -r now was acknowledged, the node became unreachable and then returned with a new boot_id (5019b2cf...) matching the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot, and post-restart checks show the anchor file intact, trust list still listing 'OS Comparison Root CA', and openssl verify still OK.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly satisfied: a self-signed 'OS Comparison Root CA' (CA:TRUE) was created on node1, installed into the system trust anchors, and confirmed functionally trusted via both trust-list presence and successful chain verification of a CA-signed leaf certificate. The mandatory restart-evidence protocol was also executed cleanly, showing a genuine reboot (boot_id change corroborated by fixed lifecycle snapshots) with the CA trust configuration intact afterward. No unnecessary or unresolved mutations were found.
limitations: Native package-health checks timed out both before and after the executor's work, so package-manager consistency could not be independently confirmed, though this predates the executor's actions and is unrelated to the CA task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two early commands failed without mutating state: cmd-8150fe807fac43c0 (mkdir without sudo, permission denied, no directory created) and cmd-0118f884240b498c (openssl x509 with an invalid -ext flag on OpenSSL 1.0.2, read-only diagnostic that produced no output change). The temporary leaf certificate/key/CSR created for end-to-end validation (cmd-b81cb513678d4b3a) was fully cleaned up immediately afterward (cmd-8db32bd32cfb4b33), leaving no residue, and the after_executor temp-file diff confirms no leftover leaf-cert artifacts. The only remaining /tmp addition (reboot.log, systemd-private dirs) is an expected byproduct of the mandated restart protocol, not executor residue. No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations were identified.
